QF.id: Analysis of Equity and Debt Instruments_25

question.text: Manish purchased listed REIT units on 01-Feb-2024 for Rs.3,00,000 and sold them on 15-Mar-2025 at Rs.3,80,000. STT was paid on the transaction. What is the capital gains treatment?

answer.text: STCG of Rs.80,000 at slab rate
LTCG of Rs.80,000 at 12.5% (above Rs.1.25L exemption)
LTCG of Rs.80,000 covered under Section 112A; no tax payable if aggregate Section 112A LTCG for the year does not exceed Rs.1,25,000
LTCG of Rs.80,000 at 12.5% without any exemption threshold

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Level 2 workbook (pages 256, 259, 280), listed REIT units sold with STT paid become long-term assets after a 12-month holding period. Manish held the units from 01-Feb-2024 to 15-Mar-2025 - approximately 13 months - so the gain is LTCG under Section 112A. Section 112A taxes LTCG above an aggregate Rs.1,25,000 threshold at 12.5%; gains within the threshold are not subject to tax. Since Rs.80,000 is below Rs.1,25,000, no tax is payable on this gain in isolation. The Trap: Option A treats the gain as STCG, but 13 months exceeds the 12-month threshold. Option D forgets the Rs.1,25,000 exemption threshold available under Section 112A. Option B states the 12.5% rate but applies it incorrectly to a Rs.80,000 gain that is fully within the exemption threshold. Note: The Rs.1,25,000 Section 112A exemption is an aggregate limit across all Section 112A gains (listed equity shares, equity-oriented MF units, REIT / InvIT units). If a client has gains from multiple such assets in the same year, aggregate them before applying the exemption.
